newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- unchanged to up 1/8.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- unchanged to up 1/8.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices finished a quiet Friday session unchanged to up about 1/8 point, market participants said.
One large bid-wanted list of about $120 million made the rounds, but besides that action the market was mostly quiet much of the day.
Muni prices got some help from a higher Treasury market, where the government long bond was up 8/32 at 99-17/32, pushing the yield down to 6.66 percent.

The focus next week is expected to be the large slate of new issues. Sales are expected to total $7 billion in 130 sales, the largest total this year, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Negotiated offerings total $5.7 billion in 60 sales, with a $2.7 billion New Jersey Economic Development Authority taxable deal through Merrill Lynch & Co. topping the list.
On the competitive side, 70 sales totaling $1.3 billion are scheduled. A $300 million Massachusettes deal on Tuesday is the largest.

In new issue action Friday, Georgia Housing Finance Authority sold $30 million of bonds that were priced at a top yield of 5.85 percent in 2028. Senior manager Smith Barney Inc. said later in the day it had the verbal award without a change in yields.
The market next week will get several key economic reports, including durable goods for May on June 25, and the First Quarter Gross Domestic Product data on June 27.

Toward the end of the week, however, traders said activity might slow ahead of the Federal Reserve policy makers meeting, which is set for early July. While the market appeared confident that the central bank would not tighten monetary policy, it still was wary.

September muni futures finished the day unchanged at 118-11/32, while September Treasury bond futures were up 11/32 to 112-17/32. The MOB spread narrowed to 186 ticks from 197 at the close on Thursday.
In the secondary market, actively quoted issues included Cleveland AMBAC 5-1/4 Certificates of Participation of 2027, which were bid at 5.53 percent, down two basis points.
Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority FGIC 5.0s of 2023 were bid at 5.49 percent, down one basis point.
